provenance.instrument: Bethel Township Zoning Ordinance of 2008 (Chapter 480 Zoning, Ord. No. 182 of 6-10-2008, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 BE2833, Township of Bethel, Delaware County (480-132D(3) and 480-41.3J record plans and deeds in Delaware County, 480-43 refers PRD plans to the Delaware County Planning Commission). District uses and figures are text in each district article. The only attachments are Appendix A and the zoning map. New Laws page: no new laws.
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 table of contents: 'Includes legislation through 12-09-2025.' New Laws: 'There are currently no known new laws for this Code.'
checks: The code has no accessory dwelling unit. Among the uses accessory to dwellings in R-1, R-3 and R-4 it lists 'Living quarters for household employees, caretakers, or watchmen' (480-41H(5), 480-47E(5), 480-52I(5), 480-136B(5)). No special exception is named for it, so it reads as a permitted accessory use. The code does not define living quarters or say whether they may have their own kitchen. Quarters with their own kitchen inside or attached to the house may be read as a second dwelling unit, which would make the house a two-family dwelling ('One or more rooms designed and equipped for one family', 480-35)

R-2 (added 2016) lists only a garage, pool, greenhouse and sheds, and offices by special exception, as uses accessory to dwellings. It allows one accessory building of at most 80 sq ft per lot, set 2 ft from the side and rear lines (480-41.4A(7), (8)). In a unified development R-2 lots may be 4,000 sq ft and 35 ft wide, with a 20 ft front yard, 15 ft on one side and 35% coverage, and a semidetached lot may have no accessory building (480-41.4B)
The code has no definition of family. A single-family dwelling is 'designed and occupied exclusively as a residence for one family' (480-35)
'In residential districts, only one principal building may be erected on each lot' (480-35 'Principal building')

Accessory buildings must be 'behind the dwelling or main building' and count toward building coverage. One may stand in one side yard if the side and rear yards are at least 7 ft (480-136, 480-137, 480-41G)

A detached private garage or barn must be 20 ft from the rear of the house, 30 ft from the rear line and 10 ft from a side line. Its height is 16 ft to the peak with a roof pitch of 3 in 12 or more, else 12 ft. Its area limit reads 'eight 860 square feet' in the online text, so the figure is not settled (480-136D)
Minor accessory buildings such as sheds are capped at 200 sq ft and 12 ft (480-136F)
Number of accessory buildings by lot size: 1 under 30,000 sq ft, 2 up to 65,340 sq ft, 3 up to 5 acres, 5 over 5 acres (480-136G)

Conversion of a single-family detached dwelling into a dwelling for more families is a special exception anywhere the general regulations reach. It needs a petition signed by owners of 60% of the frontage within 500 ft, 750 sq ft per unit, lot area per family of at least 75% of the district requirement, no outside change, public water and sewer, and a house 'with relatively little economic usefulness as a conforming use' (480-138)

Two-family detached dwellings are permitted in R-4 only on a tract of at least 10 acres, with 3,000 sq ft of lot per dwelling, public water and sewer (480-52D, 480-53B, 480-54H). The tract also needs 20% open space and community facilities, and the Board approves the mix of housing (480-54E, G, I)
Up to four nontransient roomers may rent rooms in the house or an accessory building by special exception in R-1, R-3 and R-4 (480-41H(7))

Parking: 3 spaces for every single-family dwelling unit. 'Two-family dwellings and apartments' take 1 space for a one-bedroom unit and 2 for two or three bedrooms. A fraction rounds up. At least one space must be behind the front building line in residential districts. Living quarters are not listed, so the Zoning Officer applies the most similar use (480-123A, 480-124, 480-125A, B)

Lot of record and nonconforming lots: a building may go on an undersized lot held in separate ownership if it meets the yards, unless the Zoning Hearing Board allows less by special exception (480-131, 480-132D). A lot in a recorded subdivision may be used if it has at least 40% of the required area (480-132D(3)). A lot split by a district line follows the use rules of the more restricted district (480-38B)

Variances: 480-23. No bar on a use variance. Unlisted uses: the district use lists say 'and for no other'. Only LI-1 lets uses 'of the same general natures' as its listed uses in by special exception (480-85D). A special exception or variance lapses if no permit is taken out within 6 months (480-24C)

Floodplain rules are in Chapter 222 and stream buffers in Chapter 384 (384-24). Inside an identified floodplain area new construction and substantial improvements are prohibited unless a variance is granted under Chapter 222 (222-21), and nothing new may be built within 50 ft of the top of bank of a watercourse draining over 100 acres (222-20D). A rise in the floodway needs FEMA conditional approval first (222-20B). Trailers may not be used as living quarters (Chapter 419)

The Active Adult Community Overlay (AACOD) may be applied in R-1, R-3, R-4 and T by conditional use on a tract of at least 75 acres with public sewer and water. Its households must include someone 55 or older. Its accessory uses are 'accessory only to the overall active adult community', and that list has no living quarters. A detached house lot there is 6,000 sq ft, 60 ft wide, with yards of 25 ft front, 5 ft side (20 ft for both) and 20 ft rear, 60% impervious cover, two stories and 28 ft, and 2 parking spaces (480-100, 480-101H, 480-103G, 480-104A)
Historic preservation (Chapter 239) covers only demolition of structures on the Township's historic list. It has no ADU rule

Read: Article I, Article II (480-5 to 480-24), Article IV (480-31 to 480-35), Article V, Articles VI to XIII, XV and XVI (district use and area rules, M-H and AACOD read in full), Article XVIII (parking, by screen view), Article XIX 480-130 to 480-149.2, Chapter 222 sections 16, 20, 21 and 27, Chapter 239, Chapter 384 section 24, the New Laws page and code searches. Not read: Article III, Article XVII signs, Article XX, the C-2, LI-1 and T use lists in full, the rest of Chapters 222 and 384, and Chapter 395.

term.value: living quarters for household employees, caretakers, or watchmen
term.note: Not called an accessory dwelling. Listed among the uses accessory to dwellings. Searched for accessory dwelling, in-law, accessory apartment, garage apartment, domestic employee, second dwelling, ECHO, granny, caretaker, guest house, servant, living quarters and conversion

status.note: Tied to the household. Only its own household employees, caretakers or watchmen may live there, so the quarters cannot be rented to the public. The tool has no status for employee quarters, and family only is the nearest. A permitted accessory use with no hearing named

status_outside.note: R-2, C-1, C-2, LI-1, T and M-H do not list living quarters. Of these only R-2 permits single-family houses

path.note: Listed as a use accessory to dwellings without the words 'by special exception' that items (7) and (8) carry. A zoning permit

fallback_path.note: Zoning Hearing Board, on the usual findings. No bar on a use variance

value.name: Conversion of a single-family detached house into a dwelling for more families
value.conditions: Petition signed by owners of 60% or more of the frontage on the street within 500 ft. Each unit at least 750 sq ft. Lot area per family at least 75% of the district requirement. District yards and building area met. No outside change except for safety. Parking met. Only for a house 'with relatively little economic usefulness as a conforming use'. Public water and public sewer. The Board sets the number of families. The Department of Labor and Industry must approve the plans (480-138J)

requires.condition: Petition of owners of 60% of the frontage within 500 ft, and a finding that the house has little economic usefulness as a single-family home

value.note: Lot minimums for two families read as twice 75% of the district lot with public services: 2 x 22,500 sq ft in R-1, R-3 and R-4, 2 x 7,500 sq ft in R-2

value.name: Two-family detached dwelling (R-4)
value.conditions: Permitted in R-4 on a tract of at least 10 acres, at most six dwelling units per acre. Lot area 3,000 sq ft per dwelling and width 60 ft. Front yard 25 ft, two side yards of 25 ft together and 10 ft each, rear yard 25 ft, coverage 30%, height 35 ft. Public water and public sewer. The tract needs 20% open space and community facilities, and the Board approves the mix (480-54E, G, I)
value.note: A new two-family building on a tract of 10 acres or more, not a unit added to a house

historic_bypass.note: No historic path in the zoning chapter. Chapter 239 requires a permit only to demolish a structure on the Township's historic list

value.condition: The quarters are only for household employees, caretakers or watchmen of the household. The code does not let them be rented to others.
Quarters in a separate building must be an accessory building, not a second house. 'In residential districts, only one principal building may be erected on each lot.'

Quarters inside or attached to the house with their own kitchen may be a second dwelling unit ('One or more rooms designed and equipped for one family'), making the house a two-family dwelling. A two-family dwelling is permitted only in R-4 on a tract of at least 10 acres, and R-1 and R-3 do not list it.

disputed_by.note: Living quarters for household employees, caretakers or watchmen are listed as a use accessory to the dwelling, with no form named and no kitchen rule, so quarters in or attached to the house may be read as that accessory use and not as a second dwelling unit.

value.condition: The number of accessory buildings is capped by lot size: one on a lot under 30,000 sq ft, two from 30,000 to 65,340 sq ft, three up to 5 acres and five over 5 acres. The third and later ones need 50 ft from other buildings. A lot that already has its allowed accessory buildings has no room for a new one.

In a floodway no new construction, substantial improvement or other development unless an engineering analysis shows no rise in flood levels, and no new construction or development without a DEP permit. The floodplain chapter bars hospitals, nursing homes, jails and new manufactured home parks, not houses.

'Within any identified floodplain area, any new construction or substantial improvements shall be prohibited.' Relief is a variance under Chapter 222. A pre-1979 lot partly in the special flood hazard area must place a new dwelling outside the floodplain unless that would break the district's area and bulk rules. Outside the floodplain part of the lot the rule does not reach.

'Within any identified floodplain area, no new construction or development shall be located within the area measured 50 feet landward from the top-of-bank of any watercourse with a tributary drainage area over 100 acres.' The text names no permit exception. A new building or addition on a lot in a floodplain area must stay more than 50 ft landward of the top of bank of such a watercourse.

Where a perennial or intermittent stream passes through the site, or a lake, pond or wetland is on it, the stormwater chapter asks for a riparian buffer of at least 50 ft to each side of the top of bank. On a lot that existed when the chapter was adopted, if the side or rear setback is less than 50 ft, the buffer may be cut to 25% of that setback or 25 ft, whichever is greater. It may be 25 ft with Township approval, or 10 ft by waiver where the stream greatly reduces the use of the lot. Only trails, utility lines, bridges and other uses the Township approves may be in it, and no septic system. Whether Chapter 384 reaches a given project depends on its own thresholds for regulated activities.

A semidetached house or a townhouse end unit in R-4 has one side yard of 15 ft. The R-1 figures of 25 ft on each side and 60 ft for both sides together are for a detached house and do not apply to it.

In an approved planned residential development in R-3, a detached house lot is 10,000 sq ft and 80 ft wide, with a 40 ft front yard, side yards of 10 ft each and 25 ft together, a 30 ft rear yard and 20% building area. A semidetached or end unit lot is 8,000 sq ft and 50 ft wide, and an interior townhouse lot 4,000 sq ft and 20 ft wide.

In an approved active adult community (AACOD), accessory uses are 'accessory only to the overall active adult community', and the list names no living quarters. Its households must include someone 55 or older. A detached house lot there is 6,000 sq ft and 60 ft wide, with yards of 25 ft front, 5 ft side (20 ft for both) and 20 ft rear, 60% impervious cover, two stories and 28 ft, and 2 parking spaces.

disputed_by.note: An active adult community meets every other requirement of the chapter except those Article XVI changes, and 480-101 does not say the district's own accessory uses are barred, so the living quarters listing may still reach a house lot in the community.

districts_read_no_listing.note: None of these lists living quarters. R-2 lists its own uses accessory to dwellings without them. LI-2 is named in 480-36 and its article is reserved

types_allowed.note: The listing names no form. Quarters may be in the house or in an accessory building, which must be behind the house

setback_side_ft.note: 'An accessory building may be erected within one side yard, provided that the side and rear yards are not less than seven feet each.' A detached garage or barn needs 10 ft (480-136D)

setback_rear_ft.note: A detached garage or barn needs 30 ft from the rear line (480-136D)

max_height_garage_ft.note: 'shall not exceed 16 feet in total height (top of peak), with a roof having a pitch of three inches or more to the foot, or 12 feet total height with a pitch of less than three inches'

front_yard_barred.note: 'All accessory buildings must be behind the dwelling or main building.'

value.where: A detached private garage or barn: at least 20 ft from the rear of the house. The area limit reads 'eight 860 square feet' in the online text, so it is not settled
value.note: 12 ft with a roof pitch under 3 in 12

value.where: In R-4, an accessory structure in the rear yard of a lot under 480-53B

family_only.note: Read as tied to the household. Only its household employees, caretakers or watchmen may live there. The code does not name relatives

reading.value: A single-family home needs 3 spaces for every dwelling unit. Living quarters are not listed, so the Zoning Officer applies the most similar use. Read with the single-family row, quarters that count as a dwelling unit need 3 more, 6 in all. Read as an apartment or two-family unit, they need 1 space for one bedroom or 2 for two or three bedrooms, 4 or 5 in all. Quarters that are not a dwelling unit may need no added space. A fraction rounds up, and one space must be behind the front building line
